title: Rare Galloway Bull For Sale Waikato
text:
WAIKATO, New Zealand – Those distinctive white stripes aren’t just for show. Riggit Galloway cattle, a rare sight in New Zealand, are drawing attention for their unique markings and prized genetics.
This ancient Scottish breed offers a distinctive look and is highly sought after globally.
The Galloway, originating from Scotland in the 17th century, is one of the world’s oldest meat cattle breeds. The “Riggit” variety is easily recognized by a prominent white stripe running down its spine. Some in the herd even have white bodies with dark points on their ears, feet, and noses, giving them a panda-like appearance.
Riggit Galloway cattle are an ancient Scottish breed. They are identifiable by a distinctive white stripe down their spine. Their genetics are sought after internationally, particularly in Australia and the U.S. An open day is scheduled for the Waikato stud in mid-November. A Rare Gem in the Southern Hemisphere The appeal of these animals extends beyond their striking appearance. “We have some that are red, which is quite rare in New Zealand and quite beautiful as they have red points on their ears,” shared McVerry, referring to her herd. “And the Riggit, which are solid in colour with the stripe, are quite distinctive.”
Two of the calves born on August 25. The demand for these cattle is high, with semen and embryos being sold overseas. Australia and the United States are particularly interested in acquiring these valuable genetics.
McVerry takes pride in her herd, noting that her award-winning bull and his companions are well-bred and possess gentle temperaments. “To me, he is worth everything, as every calf he produces is just outstanding,” she said, emphasizing the quality derived from imported genetics.
14-month-old Luca. She is committed to sourcing the best genetics available and offers ongoing advice to those who purchase her cattle. McVerry also highlighted the compatibility of her Galloway bulls with dairy cows, noting the premium quality meat calves they produce.
Cherrybank Riggit Galloways. This superior meat quality is attributed to the Galloway’s distinctive double-layered, wavy coat. This thick insulation keeps the animals warm, resulting in less fat stored near the skin.
Did you know? Galloway cattle are naturally polled, meaning they do not grow horns.
For those interested in learning more or potentially acquiring some of McVerry’s exceptional Galloway herd, an open day is scheduled at her Waikato stud in the middle of next month. It’s a chance to see these remarkable animals firsthand.
